newsitem.title: USA: Russia stock index of 25 top shrs launched by IFC.
newsitem.headline: Russia stock index of 25 top shrs launched by IFC.

text.p: Russia's fledgling stock market got a boost on Monday when the International Finance Corporation (IFC) launched a daily Russia index which officials said was likely to boost investment in the market.
The IFC, the private sector arm of the World Bank, also launched daily indices for Egypt and Morocco.
The Russia global index is made up of 25 top Russian shares, ranked by market capitalisation and value traded.
It includes gas monopoly RAO Gazprom GAZP.RUO, Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation.
Gazprom's shares are very illiquid but the company has said it plans to issue securities on international markets soon.
The IFC indices are widely followed by fund managers, who use them as a guide to some investments. Russian traders have eagerly anticipated the launch of the Russia index.

Alexei Telyatnikov, chief executive of the Russian Trading System electronic over-the-counter stock trading network, told a press seminar that the index would help the Russian stock market provide more liquidity for investors.

"We have already had some interest from foreign investors who were interested not in a particular stock but in the index... I think the volume brought by the IFC index will bring some more confidence and investment on to the Russian market," he said.
The RTS already has its own index of 24 leading shares.

IFC market analyst Constantinos Grigoriadis said the IFC index had risen by 128 percent in dollar terms so far this year. He said an IFC investable index for Russia could be launched in the second half of 1997.

Inclusion in the global index series is a sign the local stock market has reached certain standards of transparency. An investable index is one deemed suitable by the IFC for U.S. and European pension investment.
Russian stocks rose sharply in the run-up to President Boris Yeltsin's re-election in July but then fell sharply. Much of the ground has since been made up.

Investors cited political uncertainty when it became clear that Yeltsin, who is awaiting heart surgery, was ill and concerned over infrastructure issues, including the state of the banking system as impediments to commiting cash.

"The primary cause was political instability but the permanent presence of political instability is also a factor of stability," said Alexander Kolesnikov, deputy chairman of the Federal Commission on the Securities Market, Russia's main stock market regulator.
He said the main remaining problems concerned infrastructure but a presidential decree on developing this area was ready for signing.
In the past, investors have run into problems with share registration including secret share issues and dilutions.
Russia's stock market is still relatively small, with average daily turnover of $10-30 million.

The 25 stocks in the IFC index are Bratsk Timber, Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum, FESCO, Gazprom, Irkutskenergo, KamAZ, Komineft, LUKoil, Megionneftegaz, Moscow Telephone, Mosenergo, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, Norilsk Nickel, Novolipetsk Steel, Noyabrskneftegaz, Purneftegaz, Rostelekom, Severstal, St Petersburg Telephone, Surgutneftegaz, Tatneft, Tomskneft, Unified Energy System and Yuganskneftegaz.
